fieldValues.title: The #592 dead-orphan pattern recurred a third time, and the strengthened guard's sweep still does not reach every package-shaped tree
fieldValues.summary: Strengthening check-package-id-uniqueness.mjs to sweep resolved packages' directory trees (srs#584) immediately found three more instances of the exact #592 pattern that no prior check had seen: srs/package/spec-authoring-core/views/{spec,rationale,unified}-document-view.json, dead pre-rename orphans sharing their UUID with the live Compositions they were renamed to. The same defect class has now shown up three separate times from independent directions (#557's canonical-name collisions, #592's single orphan, and this sweep's three). The new sweep only walks the 5 directories srs/manifest.json resolves via packageRefs; it does not extend to the other package-shaped trees check-package-id-uniqueness.mjs's own assertion 3 already lists for manifest-level scanning (packages/, conformance/, docs/spec/examples/, rfcs/). A pre-rename orphan sitting in one of those trees, sharing a UUID with something live, would still be invisible to the identity guard.
evidence: srs#584 PR (the-greenman/srs#611): running the newly-added sweep against the unmodified corpus failed with 3 'definition id ... claimed twice' errors, all under srs/package/spec-authoring-core/views/

All three had the pre-RFC-036 view.json shape (outputFormats/rootType/ordering, no sections) dated 2026-05-27, identical in class to the #592 orphan (rfc-document-view.json, also 2026-05-27, also fixed by deletion)

check-package-id-uniqueness.mjs's SEARCH_ROOTS for assertion 3 (package-id-vs-name-across-trees) is ['srs','packages','conformance','docs/spec/examples','rfcs'], five entries; the new per-package directory sweep for assertion 2 (definition identity) only walks the resolvedPackages() dirs, which is 5 directories entirely inside 'srs' — it does not walk 'packages', 'conformance', 'docs/spec/examples', or 'rfcs' at all
fieldValues.body: Not fixed in srs#584/PR #611 — that unit's assigned scope was the two blind spots named in the issue's own comments (canonical name; undeclared-in-manifest files within resolved packages). Extending the on-disk sweep to the other package-shaped trees is a natural follow-up but changes the check's performance/scope profile (rfcs/ and conformance/ are large and hold many intentionally-historical duplicate ids), so it should be its own sized unit with its own decision on which trees to include, not folded into this one silently.
